title: Google brings Swift to the backend with its own Cloud SDK
key_facts: Google has released Google Cloud API Client Libraries for Swift, for server-side use.
The libraries target Swift 6.2 and later and use SwiftNIO asynchronous event loops, HTTP/2 multiplexing and gRPC transport.
Google's Karl Weinmeister and Carlos O'Ryan say Swift 6 with strict concurrency checking has become a viable systems and cloud language.
The SDK is aimed at servers, containers and DevOps, with web frameworks such as Hummingbird or Vapor.
Swift ranked 9th on the TIOBE index in January 2020 and ranks 18th now; Stack Overflow's 2025 survey has it 20th.
IBM backed away from its server-side Swift commitment in 2019; Amazon has done little with its Smoke Framework recently.
The Register notes adoption on the server has been slow and questions how much language ergonomics will matter as AI coding agents write more code.
quote_evidence: Google has taken note and has just rolled out Google Cloud API Client Libraries for Swift, evidently convinced Swift has a backend role thanks to its performance and ease of use.
"For years, Swift was perceived mainly as a UI language tied to Apple client devices," said Karl Weinmeister, director of developer relations, and Carlos O'Ryan, software engineer, in a blog post.
Even so, server-side adoption of Swift has been slow.
why_it_matters_hint: Swift developers get an official Google Cloud client library, but server-side Swift adoption has been slow.
